newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods flat with players absent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods flat with players absent.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices were unchanged Monday, with market players absent at the annual industry conference in Texas, brokers said.
"Ninety percent of the people out here were gone," one broker said.

The few remaining players were sidelined by a downturn in energy futures markets. NYMEX crude, which expires Thursday, fell 37 cents a barrel to $20.92 while gasoline dropped 0.58 cents a gallon to 64.86 a gallon.
Meanwhile, traders saw gasoline production begin to pick up, with Mobil's Torrance refinery and Exxon's Benecia plant close to full capacity after spring maintenance shutdowns.
The increased gasoline output comes after last week's inventory survey from the American Petroleum Institute (API), which reported stocks 4.0 million barrel lower than year-ago on the West Coast.
One broker said refiners would need to operate at normal capacity for two weeks before whole prices would begin to ease.
